## Highlights

### `ak sysinfo`: the device's "About phone" in one place

Model, Android version and security patch, build, hardware serial, IMEI (both on dual-SIM devices), Android ID, Wi-Fi IP, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth MACs, CPU ABI and screen size. Values a device doesn't expose are `-`. `-a` covers every connected device and `--json` prints an array. `ak mac` still works but is now part of `sysinfo` and hidden from the help.

### `ak info` shows more

Whether the app is a system app and enabled, install and update times, the APK path (with split count), UID, and PID while it runs. The package name is now the first line on stdout, and SDK levels say which Android they are (`34 (Android 14)`). `--json` only adds keys.

### One output style across commands

- A result names its target once: `==> App info on <device>`, `✓ Restarted on <device>`
- Saved files (`screenshot`, `record`, `extract`, `pull`) print their absolute path on stdout and show where they went in the `✓` line
- `✓` details are always `(device, size, time)`; times read `120ms` / `1.2s`
- Every failure reads `Couldn't …` and names the device; every `Hint:` is one instruction you can run
- An empty result (`No recent files…`) exits 0 instead of failing

Scripts that parse the text output may need updating; `--json` output is unchanged apart from new keys.
